verses.text: Abram went up out of Egypt — he, his wife, all that he had, and Lot with him — into the South.
Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
He went on his journeys from the South even to Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
to the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first. There Abram called on Yahweh’s name.
Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, herds, and tents.
The land was not able to bear them, that they might live together; for their substance was great, so that they could not live together.
There was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. The Canaanites and the Perizzites lived in the land at that time.
Abram said to Lot, “Please, let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herdsmen and my herdsmen; for we are relatives.
Isn’t the whole land before you? Please separate yourself from me. If you go to the left hand, then I will go to the right. Or if you go to the right hand, then I will go to the left.”

Lot lifted up his eyes, and saw all the plain of the Jordan, that it was well-watered everywhere, before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of Yahweh, like the land of Egypt, as you go to Zoar.
So Lot chose the Plain of the Jordan for himself. Lot traveled east, and they separated themselves the one from the other.
Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
Now the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinners against Yahweh.
Yahweh said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, “Now, lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,
for all the land which you see, I will give to you, and to your offspring forever.
I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth, so that if a man can count the dust of the earth, then your offspring  may also be counted.
Arise, walk through the land in its length and in its width; for I will give it to you.”
Abram moved his tent, and came and lived by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built an altar there to Yahweh.

footnotes.content: After going down into Egypt in a moment of fear, Abram is now going up again. I have learned the same lesson: the Lord often brings His people back to where they once leaned on Him, not to shame them, but to restore them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram comes back richer in livestock, silver, and gold, yet the wealth that truly matters is the God who brought him back. The Lord can restore material things, but He is ever more faithful to restore our trust in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram retraces his steps to Bethel, the very place of his former tent. I find such tenderness in that: the God who met us at first still draws us back to the places where we first called on His name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is the altar Abram had built at Bethel long before. For one who knows the mercy of God through Jesus Christ, returning to worship is never a performance, but a homecoming to the One who has always been faithful to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot went with Abram, and the Lord had blessed them both. I have seen how shared blessings can become strained when our eyes turn more to what we possess than to the God who gave it all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land could not bear them both. Our resources may be limited, but God's faithfulness is not; He is the One who always has room to provide for those who trust Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Strife arose between herdsmen, and all the while the Canaanites and Perizzites looked on. How often our quarrels give the watching world reason to doubt the God who has called us to peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram appeals to Lot as family, urging peace for the sake of their relationship. In Christ we are truly family, and that makes our pursuit of peace with one another all the more urgent and precious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram lets Lot choose first, relinquishing his rights as the elder. I have learned from my Lord Jesus, who though He was first, humbled Himself for us, that true greatness is found in generous humility.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot looked with his eyes and saw a garden-like plain, forgetting that beauty can mask ruin. How easy it is to choose what looks like Eden while the God who sees all already knows the coming judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot chose for himself, going east toward the cities of the plain. I have found that choosing by sight rather than by faith often leads us closer to danger than we ever intended to go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram remained in Canaan, while Lot pitched his tent near Sodom. The man of faith stayed where God had called him, but Lot slowly drew nearer to a wicked city until it would be hard to leave.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinners against Yahweh. I am grateful that our hope is not in the righteousness of cities, but in the perfect righteousness of Jesus Christ who bore our sins for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After Lot was separated from him, the Lord speaks to Abram again with fresh promise. The God who gave up His rights for us is faithful to renew His promises to His people when we walk in faith and peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord promises all the land to Abram and to his offspring forever. For those united to Jesus, the true Seed, we look beyond Canaan to a better country, an eternal inheritance that cannot perish.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's promise of offspring like the dust of the earth seemed impossible to Abram's eyes. Yet the God who keeps His word has already begun to fulfill it in Jesus, and through Him to a multitude no one can count.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh tells Abram to arise and walk through the land. Faith doesn't just believe the promise; by God's grace it walks in it, looking to the One who is both the Giver and the Guarantee of every blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram moves his tent to the oaks of Mamre at Hebron and builds another altar to Yahweh. After all the choosing, the inheritance of faith is still this: to dwell near the Lord and to worship Him there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
